common_name: Jane Platt Dwarf Fothergilla (Low-Spreading Witch Alder)

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in spring or fall in moist, acidic, well-drained soil in partial shade to full sun; Jane Platt's low, wide-spreading habit suits it to woodland edges and small-space foundation plantings better than taller Fothergilla selections.

directions: Named for noted Portland, Oregon plantswoman Jane Platt, this dwarf witch alder selection is valued for a distinctly low, mounding, and slowly spreading habit that stays wider than tall, filling in as an unusually graceful low shrub or informal groundcover at a woodland margin. In early spring, before the blue-green leaves emerge, it produces the species' signature fragrant white bottlebrush flower spikes, generally more slender and dainty than those of straight-species plants, followed by good yellow, orange, and red fall foliage color. Give it consistently moist, humus-rich, acidic soil, since Fothergilla suffers in dry or alkaline ground, and site it where its spreading habit has room to fill in without being crowded by larger neighbors. Minimal pruning is needed beyond removing dead wood, as this selection stays naturally tidy and compact for decades.
sources: North Carolina State Extension Plant Toolbox
